name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+24 partisan lean anchors a large Democratic edge
Adams holds a massive cash advantage: about $494,000 versus $3 for Codiga
Incumbency and a favorable political environment reinforce the fundamentals
No polls or expert ratings; markets price roughly a 96% Democratic win
model.rationale: The district's 24-point Democratic lean, Adams' incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising gap — nearly half a million dollars against essentially none — point to an easy Democratic hold, and prediction markets agree at about 96 percent.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or fresh polling showing a far tighter race would be the main signals that could move this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 12th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 24 points. Representative Alma Adams is seeking re-election with about $494,000 on hand, while Republican Jack Codiga has raised under $29,000 and reported just $3 in cash. No outside groups are spending in the race, and no general-election polls or expert ratings are available.

The outlook rests on district fundamentals: the heavy Democratic lean, Adams' incumbency advantage, and the lopsided financial picture. Prediction markets price the Democratic chance at about 96 percent. The expected margin is roughly 26 points, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, though the structural advantages make a Republican upset very unlikely.
